title: Normalization of a nonempty integral open subscheme
statement: Let k be a field, C and D integral schemes, f:C→Spec k locally of finite type, and a:D→C an open immersion [def-weil-field, def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-open-immersion]. For their normalizations ν_C and ν_D [def-sc-normalization], there exists an open immersion j:D-normalization→C-normalization with dense image and j followed by ν_C equal to ν_D followed by a.

source.place: Tags 035K, 035Q and 0BXC; normalization and restriction to opens, applied to the omitted dense-open restriction in Varieties Tag 0GK5

proof.text: Normalize C and pull its finite normalization back along a to get p:N→D. The other projection r:N→C-normalization is open. The finite surjective p makes N nonempty, so N is integral. Normal stalks on C-normalization transfer through r. Normality of absolute normalization follows by applying relative-normalization normality to Spec of the function field.

Choose nonempty opens UC in C and UD in D over which their normalization maps are isomorphisms. The inverse image of UC in D is nonempty since a has nonempty open image in the integral C. Its intersection U with UD is nonempty. The pullback p and ν_D are isomorphisms over U; their inverse images of U are nonempty open subsets of integral schemes, hence dense.

Apply finite_normal_iso_of_dense_open to ν_D and p and their common isomorphism over U. Compose the resulting isomorphism D-normalization≅N with r. Its nonempty open image in the integral C-normalization is dense. The comparison equation and the pullback equation give j;ν_C=ν_D;a.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_integral_normalization_open
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (C D : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral C] [IsIntegral D]
    (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType f]
    (a : D ⟶ C) [IsOpenImmersion a] :
    ∃ j : D.normalization ⟶ C.normalization,
      IsOpenImmersion j ∧ DenseRange j ∧ j ≫ C.fromNormalization = D.fromNormalization ≫ a
